Visioner BIG | 🇺🇸 🇮🇷 🇮🇱 ‼️ ‼️ President Donald Trump says the US war against Iran is funded through the end of January, warning that Democrats could turn what he describes as a potential “total victory” into a defeat by forcing an end to the conflict. Speaking to the New York Post, Trump said Israel’s objective of bringing about regime change in Iran was “probably possible,” but insisted that removing Tehran’s leadership had never been his primary goal. Instead, he emphasized preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons. Trump also said he had never been firmly in favor of or opposed to regime change, leaving open questions about Washington’s broader objectives as the war continues. Trump’s remarks highlight the growing importance of domestic political pressure in shaping US military operations against Iran. While Washington and Israel may share concerns about Iran’s nuclear capabilities, their objectives are not necessarily identical. The administration now faces the challenge of defining what victory would mean and whether its military campaign can achieve that outcome before political and financial pressures intensify. Visioner BIG | 🇮🇹 🇺🇦 ‼️ ‼️ Italy is reportedly considering transferring between 10 and 20 Eurofighter Typhoon fighter jets to Ukraine, potentially giving Kyiv another Western combat aircraft platform to strengthen its air force. According to the Italian newspaper La Repubblica, discussions concern early-production Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft from the Tranche 1 series. These are older versions of the European multirole fighter, with more limited capabilities than later variants. No final decision, delivery schedule, or agreement on the number of aircraft has been announced. Even older Eurofighter Typhoons could strengthen Ukraine’s air defense capabilities, particularly in missions against Russian aircraft and aerial threats. However, introducing another fighter type would require additional pilot training, maintenance infrastructure, spare parts, and compatible weapons. The military value of a potential transfer would depend heavily on the aircraft’s condition, available armament, and how quickly Ukraine could bring them into service. Rémy Cointreau plans to streamline up to 15% of their staff in an attempt to increase profitability, Le Figaro reports, citing the French alcoholic beverages major. Job cuts will affect up to 14% of the staff in France and up to 16% in other countries. The company is bottling in particular Remy Martin and Louis XIII cognacs, Cointreau liqueur, and St-Rémy and Metaxa brandies.
